items.title: Adani Group eyes airline investments months after ruling out airline entry
items.rss_summary: The diversified Adani group, which runs multiple airports across the country, has requested the government to allow it to invest in the airline sector, a top official said on Friday. Group chief finance officer Jugeshinder Robbie Singh told reporters that over 60 crore people in the country can fly, and the number of daily flights needs to go up by nearly 10 times to 30,000. "And that's why we requested the government to at least allow us to invest, so that we can facilitate the development of airlines. Some fund, some other airline company and things like that...or an entrepreneur who wants to go into that space," the CFO said while speaking on the sidelines of the India Debt Capital Market Summit here. In July this year, the group said it was "not evaluating any proposal to enter the airlines business". The new infrastructure is expected to improve manufacturing flexibility, inventory management and supply reliability, while allowing BPCL to respond more efficiently to changing customer requirements and market demand. items.title: Sebi aims to cut FPI onboarding time to five business days: Chairman
items.rss_summary: Markets regulator Sebi is aiming to reduce the onboarding time for Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) from several months to as little as five business days through digital workflows and system integration, its chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said on Friday. Addressing the 17th Capital Markets Conference organised by ASSOCHAM, Pandey said the regulator has also proposed removing the additional disclosure framework for FPIs, bringing India's regulatory framework closer to global standards. "Through digital workflows and system integration, we aim to cut FPI onboarding from months to as little as five business days," Pandey said. Over the past few months, Sebi has taken several measures to ease the compliance burden for FPIs. Under the SWAGAT-FI (Single Window Automatic and Generalised Access for Trusted Foreign Investors) initiative, around 740 FPIs, accounting for nearly 17 per cent of FPI assets under custody, have registered. items.title: Britannia Industries CMO Puneet Das quits within 10 months of joining
items.rss_summary: Leading bakery foods company Britannia Industries on Friday said its Chief Marketing Officer, Puneet Das, has resigned to pursue an opportunity outside the organisation, according to a regulatory filing. Das, who joined Britannia in February 2026, will be relieved from the company's services with effect from the close of business on December 9, 2026, according to a regulatory filing. "Puneet Das, Chief Marketing Officer, has decided to pursue an opportunity outside Britannia and has resigned from the services of the Company," said Britannia. Das was appointed Chief Marketing Officer of Britannia Industries effective February 16, 2026. His exit comes less than 10 months after taking charge of the marketing function at the biscuit and bakery major.

items.title: Nestle India receives ₹36.36 lakh EPFO demand, including ₹20 lakh penalty
items.rss_summary: FMCG major Nestle India on Friday said it has received a demand of Rs 36.36 lakh from the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), including damages and a penalty of over Rs 20 lakh for the period 2012-2019. The order has been issued by the Regional Office of EPFO, Mysuru, under section 7Q and 14B of the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952, the company said in a regulatory filing. "The company has received an order from the Regional Office of Employees' Provident Fund Organisation demanding an amount of Rs 36,36,548, which includes an amount of Rs 20,09,516 on account of damages/penalty for the period of 2012-2019 under PF Code," it said. The order, received by the company on November 26, 2026, has no material impact on its financials, operations or other activities, the filing added. items.title: Sebi takes minority shareholders' rights seriously: Chairman Tuhin Pandey
items.rss_summary: Sebi Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey on Friday said the market regulator takes minority shareholders' interests very seriously and supports the role of proxy advisory firms in flagging governance concerns. Investor protection remains one of Sebi's key priorities, Pandey said. When asked about the Tata Steel-APL Apollo Tubes proposed deal, he said proxy advisory firms have every right to raise issues concerning minority shareholders, adding that public discussions and media scrutiny of such concerns are welcome. "Minority shareholders' interest is very important to us. Proxy advisers have every right to bring issues to the fore. They represent minority shareholders, and we support them when they raise such concerns. Investor protection is one of the most important things for us," Pandey said on the sidelines of an event here.
